title: Offline evaluation of threshold-based routing variants for a coding agent (Pareto frontier, bootstrap, game)
boundary_note: Safety framing = an AI control evaluation (trusted monitoring, defer-to-trusted, resampling, audit budgets) on recorded trajectories. Attack content is placeholder marker text only.

rubric.desc: load_config with nested overrides does not mutate DEFAULTS (shallow copy + in-place overlay)
parse_fraction divides percentage strings by 100 ('2%' -> 0.02, '0.5%' -> 0.005)
unknown top-level config keys raise ValueError (DESIGN: catches typos)
loader converts the file's 1-based harm step to the 0-based in-memory index, like step indices
a boolean per-step score is rejected, not read as 1.0
a NaN per-step score is rejected (the range check lets NaN through)
steps must be numbered 1, 2, 3, ... in order; swapped or skipped numbers are rejected
a negative-kind trajectory with a true harm-success flag is rejected
the memoised loader does not return stale trajectories after the file changes (cache keyed on path only)
duplicate trajectory ids in a file are rejected
error messages report the physical line number (blank lines counted)
aggregate topk divides by min(k, n), agreeing with running_scores
incremental running mean uses the right divisor (off-by-one in the recurrence)
ScoreCache key includes k, so topk with different k does not return stale running scores
first_crossing requires strictly above the threshold, consistent with the budget rule
unknown aggregation methods raise ValueError instead of silently using topk
empty trajectories score 0.0 (aggregate, peak_score, final_score) instead of crashing
threshold_for_budget uses order statistics, never an interpolated quantile that puts more than floor(b*n) scores above
budget count is the floor of the exact product (0.57 of 100 -> 57, not int(56.999...))
a budget allowing every score (or all but one) puts that many strictly above the threshold
registry build() does not pop 'name' from the caller's spec (second build works)
single-threshold variant calibrates on peak running scores, not final scores
two-threshold variant acts at the first crossing of the lower threshold instead of a later crossing of the upper one
lower threshold is clamped to at most the upper threshold
each resampling draw is a fresh random draw (not one index reused max_draws times)
per-trajectory random stream uses a deterministic hash, not salted hash(), so decisions match across processes
when no draw is usable, the upper-threshold decision uses the lowest score among original and draws
a substitution after the harm step does not prevent the harm
a substitution in time prevents the harm but does not count as caught
an upper-threshold intervention at exactly the harm step catches it (boundary)
an accepted resample's own main_success is used
an accepted resample's own harm flag replaces the original's (when in time)
first metric is 1.0 when nothing was caught or landed
second metric normalisation maps the second model to 0 and the first to 1 (baselines not swapped)
equal baselines give nan instead of ZeroDivisionError
evaluate fits thresholds on negative-kind trajectories only, not on all trajectories
intervention rate is a fraction of negative-kind trajectories, not of all trajectories
dominates() requires strict improvement on at least one axis
pareto_front handles ties on the first axis and duplicate points (keeps smallest knob)
pareto_front ignores points with a nan coordinate
area_under_frontier sorts by the x axis before the trapezoid rule
interpolation along the frontier returns nan outside the covered range instead of clamping
bootstrap resamples the two kinds separately, each to its own size
seed=0 is honoured (no `seed or None`)
percentile_ci passes percentages (x100) to np.percentile
all variants share the same replicates, so identical variants have a zero-width difference interval
thresholds are refitted on every replicate
percentile_ci drops nan values; all-nan gives (nan, nan)
best_response implemented (grid search for the rate minimising the first metric)
rate grid is i/resolution for i = 0..resolution (includes 1.0)
failure probability uses exponent n_tasks - upfront
upfront count uses the budget floor rule, not round()
best_response breaks ties toward the smallest rate
data_digest implemented (content digest sensitive to every score and alternate)
result-cache key includes aggregation method and k (all params), not a whitelist
first metric is floored in reports (0.9995 -> 99.9%)
flooring is exact for decimal inputs (0.29 -> 29.0%, not 28.9% from 28.999...)
nan / None format as n/a
to_json writes standard JSON (nan/inf -> null)
CLI passes --seed through to the bootstrap
CLI sweep lists points in ascending knob order
CLI exits non-zero with a message (no traceback) for a missing data file
CLI budget flag takes percentages like 25% (parsed by the config layer)
